Theme

Time, the calendar & feasts

for the first time phrase

also now for the first time, then for the first time, first time, today for the first time

classical

Cic. Rep. 2.7.12: lūdōrum grātiā quōs tum prīmum anniversāriōs in circō facere cōnstituisset (Lewis & Short s.v. tum)
Ter. And. 5.4.33: post illa nunc prīmum audiō (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 315
Traupman 316, 394

prīmum

for the first time (with a word of time: tum, nunc, hodiē)

Usually with a word of time: tum prīmum, then for the first time; nunc prīmum, now for the first time; quō diē prīmum, on the day when first (Cic. Phil. 5.11.30, Lewis & Short s.v. prīmus).

Other words

  • prīmō — at first; rarely, for the first time

    also used · classical · Traupman 87: for the first time, prīmō

    Lewis & Short s.v. tum: tum prīmum, “rarely prīmō”. Prīmō is mostly “at first”, as against later (see firstly); prīmum is the clearer word.

Examples

  • pōnte sublicio tum prīmum in Tiberī factō

    the Pile Bridge having then for the first time been built over the TiberLiv. 1.33.6 (Lewis & Short s.v. tum)

See also firstly, original.
